features.notes: Pinned Compact 0.36.1 and Noctium agree on both literals, the default, negation, equality, inequality, and short-circuit conjunction and disjunction across the Boolean truth table. A checked Uint narrowing shows that both hosts skip inactive branches and reject the same active invalid operands, including nested expressions. Both source checkers reject non-Boolean operands. Matched casts cover Boolean to Field and Uint, zero and nonzero Field and Uint to Boolean, and false success and true failure in the zero-only Uint range. The native checker rejects a noncanonical Boolean field and altered active branches. Four fresh Ledger 9 / ZKIR 3.2.1 relations prove and verify using official K6 and K7 parameters. Changed return commitments fail verification.

Native Field addition, subtraction, multiplication, equality and inequality match the pinned reference at zero, one and modulus boundaries. Compact 0.36.1 and ordinary and readable Noctium circuits match mixed Field and Uint arithmetic in both operand orders, including Uint248 maxima and a zero-only Uint. Compact requires an explicit Uint-to-Field cast for mixed equality and inequality. Noctium also accepts implicit widening for those comparisons. The ordinary mixed relation proves and verifies using the official K8 parameters, and a changed return commitment fails verification. Compact rejects ordered Field comparison, inv(Field) and neg(Field). Readable nominal Field aliases retain identity over Native across inputs, bindings, arithmetic, equality, conditionals, explicit casts and outputs. Readable typed witness callbacks retain nominal Field arguments and results through same-alias arithmetic and typed outputs. Callback arguments use Native host fields, require the declared alias or an explicit cast, and reject implicit Native or distinct-alias loss. The emitted native relation passes a host session and checker with the Native argument value. Ordinary `noctium_circuit` declarations retain aliases for inputs, bindings, same-alias arithmetic, explicit casts and output checks. Attached ordinary contract entrypoints retain those labels in scalar returns, check the declared return alias, and emit Native fields. Readable nominal Field private scalar cells preserve identity across private reads, same-alias arithmetic, staging and read-after-stage. The wire and journal schema stay Native, and the value remains private until explicit disclosure. Explicit Native casts and disclosure pass; implicit and distinct-alias stage values and direct public output reject. Direct and linked scalar helper calls enforce parameter and result aliases, accept explicit casts and emit Native arguments and returns. Direct scalar ledger Cells preserve labels across constructor initialization, guarded writes, and scalar readback. Plain Native or a different Field alias requires an explicit cast. Structured helpers preserve owning Cell aliases across scalar reads, guarded writes, and artifact rebuild. Read erasure and Count-to-Amount writes reject, while matching aliases and explicit casts pass. Aggregate payloads and collection values remain open.

features.notes: Pinned compiler uses inclusive maxima internally. For ordinary Uint<0..m> and Uint<0..n>, addition returns exclusive bound m+n-1 and multiplication returns (m-1)*(n-1)+1. Subtraction retains the left maximum and asserts a nonnegative result. Focused Compact 0.36.1 and Noctium source comparisons cover arithmetic, inferred bounds, typed and literal zero, the 248-bit limit, and subtraction underflow. The transparent Compact alias is compared with the underlying Noctium type. Focused nominal alias comparisons cover arithmetic, casts and selected ledger reads and writes. Broader source contexts and complete native proof coverage remain open.

conformanceCases.result: Compact 0.36.1 and readable Noctium agree on bounded addition and explicit narrowing. The alias survives addition in both readable and low-level circuits, and typed witness calls preserve it in readable authoring. Both reject mixing distinct equal-bound types, implicit conversion to the underlying type, checked narrowing overflow and a too-wide intermediate sum. Direct and reusable-helper Cell cases and scalar List cases agree on 19 (initial), 41 (nominal write) and 255 (explicit cast and write). Both reject implicit raw UInt or mismatched-nominal List pushes. Noctium source execution and ZKIR lowering also cover nominal Lists under one and two map keys. Pinned Compact and the Noctium source evaluator agree on Map<Count, Amount> membership, lookup, upsert, explicit key and value casts, removal and nested sibling preservation. Both reject wrong nominal or raw key and value types. The same Noctium entrypoints lower to ZKIR. The Compact and Noctium Set fixtures insert Amount 19 at the root and under Count 7, read membership, and remove both entries. Equal-bound nominal types and raw values reject at the key and member positions. Noctium's structured scalar Map fixture reads 19, writes 41, and retains the value identity across a helper call. Hosted ledger callback compilation preserves the key and result identities. Compact and Noctium initialize the Position amount at 19 from checked constructors. Both observe the nominal 41 and explicitly cast 255 in root and Map records, and reject raw or wrong-nominal writes to Amount. Noctium also checks record field types through a two-key Map and through List push and head. Constructors now check both record layouts, including the finalized root Cell and Bytes32-keyed Map. Three-key record paths preserve identity through Lean source lowering. Both the pinned Compact and native checker cases return the expected Maybe record payload.
